Verified via Playwright mouse-drag simulation on https://divine-office.preview.emergentagent.com/coloring/cross with mobile viewport 390x844 and injected sanctus_session_token. All five acceptance criteria PASSED: (1) canvas screen (testID coloring-canvas-screen) loads; (2) a freehand mouse-drag over testID coloring-canvas produced one SVG stroke visible on top of the line-art (color=#E23B3B, translucent so outline still shows); (3) selecting testID coloring-color-#3E8ED0 and drawing again produced a second path with stroke=#3E8ED0; (4) testID coloring-undo removed the last stroke (2->1 paths) and testID coloring-clear removed all strokes (1->0 paths); (5) the line-art still displays (naturalWidth 1408, naturalHeight 768) from GET /api/coloring-pages. The root-cause fix (image at bottom, SVG on top with pointerEvents=none, lineArt with pointerEvents:'none' so parent PanResponder receives gestures) is working correctly on react-native-web. context_for_next_testing_agent: Coloring canvas drawing bug is fixed and verified on web preview. To reproduce the test: set viewport 390x844, inject localStorage sanctus_session_token='test_feat_aug25', navigate to /coloring/cross, then use Playwright page.mouse.down() -> multiple page.mouse.move() -> page.mouse.up() over the [data-testid="coloring-canvas"] element and count svg path elements inside it (should increase by 1 per drag). Note: react-native-web PanResponder requires a real press-drag with intermediate mousemove points; a single click does not trigger a stroke (by design - onPanResponderRelease only commits strokes containing an 'L' command).
rca_of_issue: Root cause (already fixed by main agent): the line-art <Image> component was rendered above the SVG stroke layer and, after a prior deprecation fix, lost its pointerEvents='none'. The opaque image therefore intercepted all touch/mouse events, preventing the parent PanResponder from ever receiving gestures. Additionally, SVG strokes were rendered behind the opaque image so even if a stroke had been recorded it would have been hidden. Mitigation applied: (a) render <Image> first (bottom) with style.pointerEvents:'none' via the lineArt style so it does not intercept gestures; (b) render <Svg> after (on top) with pointerEvents='none' so it also passes gestures through to the parent View; (c) the parent View (testID coloring-canvas) attaches panResponder.panHandlers and receives all gestures reliably. Verified: drag produces stroke paths in DOM, color changes reflected in stroke attribute, undo/clear work, image still displays.
